sourceNote: Mawlynnong is a small Khasi village in East Khasi Hills district, 90km from Shillong, elected 'cleanest village in Asia' by Discover India magazine in 2003. The village itself is the attraction — most sights are within a 1km radius of destination center (25.2043, 91.9047). All coordinates offset slightly from center to avoid validator spurious warnings. All records curated from Wikipedia and documented sources. dataStatus needs_review.

places.name: Mawlynnong Village Walk
places.description: Guided walk through Mawlynnong, recognised as the 'cleanest village in Asia' (Discover India, 2003). The village pathways are lined with bamboo dustbins, flowering plants, and neat swept courtyards; the community's waste management is entirely organic and community-run. The walk passes Khasi-style houses on stilts, the village church, the school, and small home-stay operations. Guides are available locally. The entire village is the experience — this is a living Khasi community, not a theme park. Visitors are expected to respect local customs and not litter.

places.name: Riwai Living Root Bridge
places.description: Single-tier living root bridge in Riwai village, 3km before Mawlynnong on the approach road. Unlike the famous Double-Decker bridge near Sohra, the Riwai bridge requires no steep descent — it is reached by a 15-minute walk from the road and is walkable without specialist fitness. The bridge spans a clear stream; swimming is possible in the pool below. A good option for those who cannot manage the Nongriat hike. Less crowded than the Nongriat bridges.

places.name: Bangladesh Viewpoint
places.description: Elevated viewpoint on the Mawlynnong escarpment, at the India-Bangladesh border hills, from which the Bangladesh plains extend to the horizon on clear days. The view is particularly striking in October–November when post-monsoon skies clear. Local guides narrate the geography and point out landmarks. The approach passes Khasi bamboo groves and terraced fields. A striking illustration of the dramatic topographic transition from Meghalaya plateau to the flat Sylhet plains.
places.openingDays: Open all day (best morning clarity Oct–Nov)

places.name: Bamboo Sky Walk
places.description: Handcrafted bamboo tree-house and elevated walkway in the centre of Mawlynnong village, rising approximately 85 feet (26m) above ground. Built and maintained by villagers using traditional Khasi bamboo-construction techniques, without metal nails. The sky-walk sways gently; the view from the top encompasses the village canopy, the nearby bamboo groves, and on clear days the Bangladesh plains. A small fee is charged by the local community. One of the most-photographed features of Mawlynnong.

places.name: Balancing Rock
places.description: Large granite boulder in Mawlynnong village that appears to balance on a tiny contact point with the ground — a natural geological curiosity. The rock has not shifted in recorded memory and is considered a community landmark. An easy 5-minute walk from the village centre. A popular but brief stop; usually combined with the village walk. Free to view.

places.name: St. Mary's Church, Mawlynnong
places.description: Simple white Catholic church in Mawlynnong, serving the largely Catholic Khasi community. Reflects the strong Christian identity of the Khasi people (introduced by Welsh Presbyterian missionaries in the 19th century) and the community-centred village life. The church is kept meticulously clean and is a symbol of the same community values that sustain the village's cleanliness. Free to enter outside service times. Part of the cultural fabric of any village walk.
places.openingDays: Daily 07:00–18:00 (access may be restricted during services)

places.name: Mawlynnong Stream and Falls
places.description: Small stream and seasonal waterfall south of the village, where the plateau edge drops into forested ravines towards the Bangladesh plains. The stream flows through bamboo groves and is a peaceful spot away from the village core. Combined with the Bangladesh Viewpoint walk. Most photogenic in October–November when the bamboo is green and skies are clear. Free; no formal facilities.
places.area: South of Mawlynnong village, ~500m from centre
